transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-24 15:00 PT | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Lina (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Samir (Northgate Procurement), Alicia (Northgate Legal), Martin (Northgate Platform), Jules (Northgate FinOps)
Summary (auto): redline handoff of MSA/DPA, SLA tiers and timing, pricing approval path; action items and next follow-up.
Topics: MSA redlines; DPA exceptions; SLA metrics and uptime tiers; pricing approvals and committed capacity; KMS/keying & egress; pilot acceptance criteria.

00:00:00 Lina (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, we've got about an hour on this. quick roll call?
00:00:06 Samir (Procurement): Samir here. Alicia?
00:00:08 Alicia (Legal): Alicia on. Martin here.
00:00:11 Marco (SE): Marco from Redwood, hi.
00:00:13 Priya (CSM): Priya on as well.
00:00:16 Jules (FinOps): Jules here.
00:00:20 Lina: cool, objective is to hand off the MSA/DPA redlines and align timeline for SLA & pricing approvals so you can present to procurement next week.
00:00:32 Samir: perfect. principle question — we need to know whether this will be hosted or private for the initial pilot; that changes egress and KMS assumptions.
00:00:44 Lina: yes, good call. pilot plan we talked about was hosted API for speed but with VPC peering option if you want private. we can offer Redwood Dedicated reserved pools if you want predictable latency and dedicated GPUs — pricing differs.
00:00:59 Martin: latency matters for our search re-rank path — 150ms P95 is sort of our soft bar. can Redwood guarantee that on hosted?
00:01:10 Marco: short answer — we operate SLOs per model and route. on hosted we tier by capacity; typical P95 for that workload is 120–160ms depending on sequence length and batching. for strict 150 we recommend a dedicated lane or reserved capacity. there was a note i wrote down about continuous batching vs your qps distribution — i'll include the numbers in the snapshot.
00:01:35 Alicia: on the legal side two quick flags in the DPA: we need subprocessors list, data residency statements, and a clear incident notification timeline — 24 hours for material incidents. also SOC2 evidence and if possible ISO.
00:01:50 Lina: we can share SOC 2 report and ISO attestation — sometimes it's a third party report; we'll send the certs. for subprocessors we have a standard registry, but if you need contract-level subprocessors clause change that's doable — please mark exact phrasing.
00:02:04 Alicia: also KMS — mandatory customer-managed key for production. we can't have provider-controlled keys for PII.
00:02:11 Marco: understood. Redwood Private supports BYOK via KMS integration and on-prem options for full key custody; hosted offers KMS integration with customer keys in some plans, we'll call that out. note: there might be an egress charge if you use your own key store depending on region.
00:02:26 Jules: egress — important. we must map egress to our FinOps buckets. can you give a representative egress model for token throughput? we need numbers not just percentages.
00:02:37 Marco: yes i'll produce a short egress table for the Pilot Search path. baseline tokens per request, tokenization rates, and a per-GB egress estimate; will also show delta for prioritizing prefix cache.
00:02:50 Samir: on SLA: we require 99.9% availability for production, with credits and an escalation ladder. are you able to commit to 99.9 for Dedicated?
00:03:01 Lina: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime — 99.9 is standard for dedicated pools. for hosted we typically offer 99.5 on lower tiers, 99.9 at enterprise tiers. we'll map pricing lanes to SLA ladders in the addendum.
00:03:15 Alicia: and liabilities — indemnity and cap — can we get a clause for data breach carve-out? our legal asks for a carve-out for gross negligence in the indemnity section.
00:03:25 Lina: we usually follow market standard caps but open to discuss carve-outs. if you mark the exact language we can take it to commercial legal.
00:03:33 Martin: small technical thing — does the runtime support KV cache export for replay and debugging? we want to be able to reproduce inference rejects locally.
00:03:41 Marco: we support KV cache snapshots for Dedicated and Private. on hosted you get logs and trace hooks but not raw KV exports because of multi-tenant concerns; however we have a replay feature that reconstructs the state. there might be PII redaction rules.
00:04:00 Alicia: about DPA exceptions — we will likely need a clause that limits cross-border processing for certain datasets; we'll provide a list.
00:04:07 Lina: ok please send the dataset categories. we'll map region and residency constraints.
00:04:12 Samir: timeline: procurement committee meets 2025-04-16. we'd like final MSA/DPA and pricing packaged two business days before. is that feasible?
00:04:22 Lina: yes, that gives us about three weeks. we'll aim to deliver redlines by 2025-04-02 so you have time to review.
00:04:30 Alicia: that works if we can push back quick questions; prefer a 1:1 with legal if we need to.
00:04:36 Priya: happy to schedule dedicated legal walk-through. we find shorter sessions speed sign-off.
00:04:41 Jules: on pricing, the commit model — we need a glide path: pilot volume, threshold for reserved commit, and how auto-scaling impacts committed spend.
00:04:51 Marco: we'll do a three-month pilot pricing sheet showing pay-as-you-go, a soft commit tier, and a reserved level for sustained throughput; include example math for cost per 1M tokens and projected savings if you enable quantization or prefix cache.
00:05:06 Samir: on pilot acceptance — what metrics do we need to sign off? availability, latency, quality (F1 or relevance), and runbook for rollback.
00:05:16 Lina: typical acceptance criteria: 1) integration smoke tests pass, 2) P95 latency below agreed threshold for three consecutive days, 3) error rate below x% and 4) quality tests on seed prompts show no regression vs baseline. we'll propose a concrete checklist.
00:05:33 Alicia: can you confirm audit logs retention? we need 12 month retention for traceability.
00:05:40 Marco: we support configurable retention; default is 90 days for hosted, enterprise tiers can extend to 12 months per add-on. we'll include the retention opt-in in the addendum.
00:05:51 Samir: procurement asks about termination notice and data return — 30 days or so?
00:05:58 Lina: typical term is 30 days data retrieval window after termination; for longer retention we can escrow or extend via addendum.
00:06:06 Alicia: export format must be JSONL and include redaction markers.
00:06:10 Marco: noted.
00:06:12 Martin: small hiccup — we use an internal feature flag system, we want Redwood to support a header-based tenant id so we can do A/B tests.
00:06:20 Marco: header-based tenancy is supported via route metadata; we can show an example in the integration guide.
00:06:28 Samir: any competitors in the procurement packet? we should state who the alternatives are; legal likes to see a market map.
00:06:34 Lina: we don't put competitors in the MSA but in commercial summary often we list alternatives. you asked earlier — OpenAI and Anthropic were in the shortlist, and some teams look at Bedrock for native cloud integration.
00:06:50 Alicia: can you provide a concise security pack: SOC2, iso, pen test summary, and subprocessor list please.
00:06:58 Priya: yes we'll attach a security bundle; i'll start a secure share and drop the artifacts.
00:07:03 Jules: any special billing terms — we want monthly invoices that line up with our FinOps tooling, and ability to map to cost centers.
00:07:10 Lina: we support invoice mapping and cost center tags via our billing API. we'll include sample invoice templates.
00:07:17 Samir: about the DPA — we may request a 24 hour incident SLA for high-severity; does Redwood have that in existing DPA language?
00:07:25 Lina: current DPA states prompt notification of incidents; for high-severity we can commit to 24 hours for notification and initial remediation plan. i'll flag that for legal.
00:07:35 Alicia: last item from me — RTO and RPO expectations for Dedicated environments? we need to ensure recovery objectives are stated.
00:07:43 Marco: for Dedicated we document RTO for node failure and regional outage; typical RTO is under 4 hours for failover paths, RPO is near zero for stateful caches if using our multi-zone replication. i'll include the specifics.
00:07:59 Samir: ok this is helpful. can we recap next steps?
00:08:03 Lina: recap: 1) Redwood to send redlined MSA+DPA+pricing addendum by 2025-04-02; 2) SE to send perf and egress snapshot by 2025-04-04; 3) security bundle posted to secure share; 4) Northgate legal to reply with clause-level feedback by 2025-04-09; 5) follow-up commercial sync week of 2025-04-14.
00:08:30 Alicia: yes, and we'll try to get procurement deck to you a week prior if possible.
00:08:35 Marco: quick question for Jules — what's your threshold for converting pilot to reserved commit? is it a monthly spend trigger or qps?
00:08:44 Jules: we prefer a monthly spend trigger, something like >$30k/month sustained for 30 days or qps above X; i'll put exact numbers in our reply.
00:08:53 Lina: great. any other issues?
00:08:56 Martin: none from infra.
00:08:58 Priya: i'll schedule the legal walkthrough for the week of 2025-04-07.
00:09:02 Lina: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll share notes and deliverables.

(occasional crosstalk and mumbled line items during doc-drafting)

00:25:12 Marco: -- i'm just noting, there is an edge-case on provisioned capacity where we may need a short maintenance window for kernel upgrades, that will be communicated 72 hours in advance and will not count against SLA.
00:25:26 Samir: please avoid scheduling during peak campaigns.
00:25:29 Marco: understood.
00:38:05 Lina: closing thoughts — we want to make this lightweight to get you running; legal and procurement are the gating items.
00:38:14 Alicia: agree. thanks for the clarity.
00:38:20 Lina: action items we'll capture and drop in the calendar. thanks all.

Meeting end: 15:58 PT
